text.name: fabrix_help_overview_title
text.text: FabriX - new gameplay for your productions

text.name: fabrix_help_overview_intro_text
text.text: Until now, factories ran on autopilot: unload inputs, switch on, cash in. FabriX turns them into real businesses that challenge you as the director.

text.name: fabrix_help_overview_before_tasks_text
text.text:
No more flat costs: your buildings consume real electricity and water. Monthly wages, transparent transport costs and the yearly property tax land on your bill, itemised exactly.
Above all, your staff count: without employees, not a single wheel turns. Staff your shifts cleverly – the more experienced the team, the higher the output. Hire skilled workers, train apprentices and level up your people through experience points (XP). But watch out: more performance also means higher salary demands. If space runs out, you simply upgrade your factories.

text.name: fabrix_help_overview_features_text
text.text: Keep your factories fully utilised at all times, because idle time burns hard cash. Coordinate shifts, manage training and keep your running costs firmly under control.

text.name: fabrix_help_gui_open_text
text.text: Press [K] to open and close your company headquarters (key binding can be changed in the control settings). The menu is divided into four sections: Overview, Shift plan, Employees and Job market.

text.name: fabrix_help_gui_overview_text
text.text:
Your control center for all key figures: workforce size, active factories, shift utilisation, overall efficiency and running fixed costs at a glance.
On top of that, the system raises the alarm immediately when there are bottlenecks: vacant shifts, missing Masters or Directors, sick notes, upcoming retirements or employees ready for training are reported directly. You also see immediately which factory is at a standstill – whether due to a lack of staff, inactive recipes, low inputs (below 20 %) or overflowing storage.
Under "Notifications" you can switch off messages about promotion & training, sickness and staff changes for yourself.

text.name: fabrix_help_gui_shiftplan_text
text.text: Here you coordinate the three-shift system of your factories. Fill workplaces flexibly with staff, assign leaders to the factory and keep an eye on the productivity of every single shift in real time. At the top right you see the factory's experience and start the upgrade.

text.name: fabrix_help_gui_employees_text
text.text: The HR office: check level, experience, wage costs, age and workplace of your team. Send skilled workers on training, manage dismissals or renegotiate salaries if staff want to leave (chances of success vary). The “Sick” section shows all current staff absences.

text.name: fabrix_help_gui_market_text
text.text:
Recruit new staff from three applicant groups: seasonal workers (starting level 1–3), apprentices and skilled workers (usually Journeymen). Each placement costs a €250 hiring fee.
Beware of hasty dismissals: quick “hire and fire” gets expensive, because severance payments are due on dismissal. From a business point of view, it often pays off to keep staff on the payroll even in weak months.
The applicant pool is topped up monthly and completely renewed at every change of season (March, June, September, December). More factories attract more applicants.
Special case apprentices: apprenticeships start exclusively from July to September. You need at least one factory at level 3, because apprentices strictly need a Master on site for supervision.
In multiplayer, each farm has a completely separate job market and its own staff.

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_shifts_text
text.text:
Factories produce 24/7 across three 8-hour shifts: Early shift: 00:00–08:00 Day shift: 08:00–16:00 Late shift: 16:00–24:00
The available slots grow with the factory level. Staff can only work in one single shift per day – a change during or after a shift is blocked for that day.
The shift output is the summed productivity of the workers present (100 % equals the standard speed of the base game). Three pros with 120 % throughput each therefore speed up production 3.6-fold. Vacant shifts mean the factory stands still.

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_categories_text
text.text:
As soon as the lines are running, assigned employees gain experience (XP). With every level, their productivity and their salary demands rise.
Seasonal workers form your flexible core workforce. Skilled workers follow the career path from Journeyman via Master to Director – indispensable, because larger factories strictly require leaders. Apprentices start cheap with low productivity. They work exclusively in the day shift of factories from level 3, under the supervision of a Master.

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_seasonal_text
text.text: Seasonal workers level up to level 10 and increase their output by almost 50 % along the way. Ideal for flexibly absorbing peaks in demand in standard factories.

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_career_text
text.text:
Once they have enough practical experience, apprentices complete three school phases automatically and graduate as Journeymen.
You send experienced skilled workers on further training manually: Journeyman to Master: 6-month course (€3,000) Master to Director: 8-month course (€6,000)
During the course, shift work pauses with full continued pay. Afterwards, you assign the skilled worker again.
No apprentices available on the job market? They only apply in late summer (July–September) and require at least one factory of your own at level 3 that is authorised to train.

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_salary_text
text.text:
Salaries are settled monthly. The base salary is €100 for seasonal workers and €80 for apprentices and skilled workers, calculated before level surcharges.
Recruits from the market demand hefty salary surcharges: seasonal workers +10–40 %, skilled workers +10–70 %. Apprentices keep their low base wage even after further training.
Example Director: home-grown: €176/month | poached from the job market: €194–299/month.

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_tip_text
text.text:
Skilled workers you train yourself save huge sums in the long run. In addition, Masters and Directors are extremely rare on the open market (only approx. 6 % of applicants).
Development time: Apprentice to Journeyman: approx. 3 years
So secure apprentices early, as soon as your first factory reaches level 3, and make sure they get regular shifts.

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_leaders_text
text.text:
Large factories require leadership structures (they work outside the regular shift slots): Master (from factory level 3, level 7–9): actively lends a hand in the day shift and enables apprentice training. Director (from factory level 5, level 10): purely administrative – cuts the site's property tax drastically by 75 %.
Level 5 factories require both a Master and a Director. If either role is missing, the entire factory grinds to a halt.

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_dismissal_text
text.text:
At 65, the well-earned retirement follows, without severance. If, on the other hand, you dismiss employees for operational reasons, a severance of €50 per month of employment is due at the end of the notice period (wages continue until then; XP gain and courses are blocked).
Notice periods: seasonal workers (end of month), Journeyman (3 months), Master (6 months), Director (9 months). Apprentices are protected against dismissal.
Regret is costly: withdrawing a dismissal is expensive (seasonal worker €1,500, Journeyman €3,000, Master €6,000, Director €10,000).

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_absence_text
text.text:
Short-notice sick leave blocks shift or leadership slots while wages continue to be paid. If the Master is sick and there is no replacement, the factory stands still. Recovered employees must be put back on the roster manually.
Unplanned idle time provokes resignations: neglected staff throw in the towel (without severance). Prevent them from leaving with a salary increase (+10 % to +100 %). You have exactly one negotiation attempt – if you decline or the offer fails, the skilled worker is gone.

text.name: fabrix_help_employees_apprentice_text
text.text: Regular training takes 3 years. If you leave apprentices to rot on the bench, the law steps in: after 4 years, a €500 late penalty is due. After 5 years, the apprentice drops out – costing you a €2,500 fine plus €15,000 compensation. Shift assignments are mandatory!

text.name: fabrix_help_factories_xp_text
text.text:
Active factories with staffed shifts gain up to 10 XP per month. As soon as the XP bar is full, you can modernise the site for a fee. You start the upgrade in the shift plan with the X key.
Attention, construction phase: during the renovation, production stops completely. After completion, the factory must be reactivated manually in the production menu.

text.name: fabrix_help_factories_benefits_text
text.text: Each level enlarges your storage, creates more workplaces per shift and, from level 3, unlocks training your own young talent.

text.name: fabrix_help_factories_levels_text
text.text: Level 1: base factory | storage 1.0x | 1 slot/shift Level 2: 80 XP | €30,000 | 1 month renovation | storage 2.0x | 2 slots/shift Level 3: 110 XP | €80,000 | 2 months renovation | storage 3.5x | 3 slots/shift + Master Level 4: 210 XP | €120,000 | 3 months renovation | storage 5.0x | 4 slots/shift + Master Level 5: 330 XP | €250,000 | 3 months renovation | storage 7.5x | 5 slots/shift + Master & Director

text.name: fabrix_help_factories_important_text
text.text: Upgrade cost trap: from level 3 the factory strictly requires a Master, from level 5 additionally a Director. If the leaders are missing, productivity drops to a flat 0 %. Be sure to plan suitable skilled workers before the upgrade.

text.name: fabrix_help_auto_function_text
text.text:
From factory level 2, automatic shift scheduling is available to you (can be activated separately for each factory). The system fills free slots on its own by priority: first apprentices, then skilled workers and finally seasonal workers – each sorted by highest individual productivity.
If staff are absent due to sickness or courses, a replacement moves up automatically.

text.name: fabrix_help_auto_leaders_text
text.text:
Leadership positions have top priority: if a Master or Director post becomes vacant, the system fills it immediately. If necessary, leaders are pulled from regular shifts for this (even from other factories). An active factory leadership, however, is never touched.
Priority for apprentices: from level 3, Auto mode automatically pushes available apprentices into the day shift. If it is fully staffed, a regular employee has to make way – they move either to another free slot or back into the staff pool.

text.name: fabrix_help_auto_notes_text
text.text:
Manual changes lock the slot: if you remove staff by hand, Auto mode only acts on this slot again after the next day change (midnight).
Construction-site logic: factories under renovation receive no new staff; however, the system can move employees who are unused there to other factories.
Deactivation: if you switch the mode off or clear all slots via the button, automatic scheduling stops immediately.

text.name: fabrix_help_auto_costs_text
text.text: Automated scheduling costs €150 per factory and month. The amount is settled at the end of the month together with the salaries.

text.name: fabrix_help_revamp_title
text.text: Compatibility with the Production Revamp mod

text.name: fabrix_help_revamp_compatibility_text
text.text: FabriX and Production Revamp can be used at the same time. FabriX (version 1.0.0.0) was tested with Production Revamp (version 1.0.0.0). However, completely error-free operation cannot be guaranteed.

text.name: fabrix_help_revamp_limitations_text
text.text:
Transportation costs: When used together, Production Revamp handles distribution between productions and calculates transportation costs. Therefore, the FabriX transportation-cost entry remains empty.
Renovation: Production lines with “autoStart” or “hideFromMenu” in their production XML cannot be switched off by Production Revamp and may keep running during a factory upgrade.

text.name: fabrix_help_other_costs_text
text.text:
Full transparency instead of flat rates: FabriX itemises all operating and staff costs as separate entries in your financial overview.
Billing intervals: Monthly: salaries as well as electricity (€0.35/kWh) and water (€5.45/m³), calculated exactly according to active recipes. Daily: logistics costs in “Distribute” mode. Yearly: property tax (€80–800 per factory; a Director reduces it by 75 %). As needed: hiring (€250), courses (€3,000 / €6,000), upgrades (€30,000–250,000 as investment), severance and late penalties.
Compatibility: base game factories use fixed consumption values for electricity and water. For factories from external mods, FabriX automatically determines dynamic consumption amounts.

text.name: fabrix_help_other_production_text
text.text: When the lines stand still, check the following points: 1. Inputs: does the input storage have enough supply? 2. Capacity: is the output storage full? 3. Status: are the relevant recipes set to active in the menu? 4. Shift plan: is the current shift fully staffed? 5. Leadership: is the Master missing from level 3 or the Director from level 5?

text.name: fabrix_help_other_limits_text
text.text: Multiplayer: system messages follow the language setting of the host or server. FabriX was successfully testen on Dedicated servers. Despite intensive testing, bugs cannot always be ruled out.

text.name: fabrix_help_other_feedback_text
text.text: Found bugs, feedback on balance or new ideas? Feel free to open a detailed issue directly in the GitHub repository: https://github.com/Manu100001/FS25_FabriX
